newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: RUGBY UNION-LIONS NARROWLY AVOID DEFEAT IN MUDBATH.
newsitem.headline: RUGBY UNION-LIONS NARROWLY AVOID DEFEAT IN MUDBATH.

text.p: A try seven minutes from time by skipper Rob Wainwright saved the British Lions from defeat by Border in an East London mudbath on Wednesday.
In treacherous, sodden conditions the Lions trailed 14-10 going into the final quarter and a repeat of Border's 1955 victory over the tourists looked a distinct possibility.
The Lions had made their own problems with a disjointed performance in the back division and only one successful kick out of eight at goal.
A Border try by left-wing Andre Claasen just before halftime and three successful penalties from four attempts by fly-half Greg Miller had put Border ahead with 12 minutes remaining.
The Lions had struggled to control possession but they finally forced a lineout in the right hand corner. Lock Doddie Weir won possession and Wainwright was driven over by his pack from two metres.
The desperate closing moments were in contrast to a bright opening from the Lions who demonstrated their determination to run the ball despite the conditions.
In the third minute they quickly moved the ball down the backline into the Border 22 to make room for right wing John Bentley to dive over in the corner.
Miller narrowed the gap with a penalty shortly afterwards before the game descended into a mudddy slog before hooker Mark Regan scored the Lions' second try.

Number eight Eric Miller drove from the base of a scrum and, when he was held, Regan was the first man in support to be driven over for a carbon copy try to Weir's in Saturday's 39-11 victory over an Eastern Province Invitation XV.
Border rarely looked like crossing the Lions' line but Claasen was given the room to scoot over in the left corner after the ball went to ground on the Lions 22.
Miller put Border ahead with his second penalty two minutes after the interval and his third made it 14-10 to the home side in the 68th minute.
The Lions were disrupted when Scott Gibbs -- their Welsh centre -- had to be stretchered off with suspected ankle ligament damage although replacement Allan Tait immediately looked the part.
He had a hand in the attack which set up field position for the clinching try before Tim Stimpson kicked a penalty on the final whistle.
The Lions are next in action against Western Province in Cape Town on Saturday.

Border - 15-Russell Bennett, 14-Kelly Hilton-Green, 13-Greg Hechter, 12-Kaya Malotana (David Maidza, 44), 11-Andre Claasen, 10-Greg Miller, 9-John Bradbrook, 8-Andre Fox, 7-Anton Botha (Deon Coetzer, 80), 6-Marius Swart, 5-Johan Gehring, 4-Streicher Boha, 3-Delarey du Preez, 2-Ruhan van Zyl (captain), 1-Heinrich Kok.

British Lions - 15-Tim Stimpson, 14-John Bentley, 13-Allan Bateman, 12-Scott Gibbs (Allan Tait, 44), 11-Tony Underwood, 10-Paul Grayson, 9-Austin Healey (Matt Dawson, 54), 8-Eric Millar, 7-Neil Back, 6-Rob Wainwright (captain), 5-Jeremy Davidson, 4-Dodie Weir, 3-David Young (Paul Wallace, 68), 2-Mark Regan, 1-Graham Rowntree.
